hints.title: Find the two remainders
hints.body: For a divisor x−t, the remainder is f(t). Set each given divisor equal to zero to find its input.
hints.recap: The remainder theorem avoids carrying out polynomial division.
hints.pitfall: A plus sign in the divisor gives a negative input.
hints.pause: Substitute both inputs, then subtract the remainders.

recall.reminder: The remainder theorem avoids carrying out polynomial division.

hints.title: Choose the constants after subtracting
hints.body: Look at the sign multiplying each letter in your simplified difference. Decide which letter should be as large or as small as possible.
hints.recap: The best value must be possible under all the restrictions.
hints.pitfall: The three letters must take different values.
hints.pause: Give an allowed assignment and calculate its difference.

recall.reminder: The best value must be possible under all the restrictions.

solution:
1. Use the remainder theorem. R=f(−2)=−8+4a−2b+c and S=f(−3)=−27+9a−3b+c.

2. Subtract first. R−S=19−5a+b. The constant c cancels.

3. Bound and attain. Since a≥1 and b≤3, R−S≤19−5(1)+3=17. The assignment (a,b,c)=(1,3,2) obeys the distinctness condition and attains this bound. Answer D: 17.
knowledgePattern: Use two remainder evaluations and maximise their difference over distinct coefficients
